citation.authors: Mori K, Inatomi S, Ouchi K, Azumi Y et al

cited_by.title: Lion's mane and reishi mushroom supplements

record.population: Japanese men and women aged 50 to 80 with mild cognitive impairment
record.design: Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of lion's mane (Yamabushitake) tablets, 3 g a day for 16 weeks, with 4 weeks of follow-up
record.finding: Cognitive scores rose more in the lion's mane group at weeks 8, 12 and 16, then fell back four weeks after stopping. Laboratory tests showed no adverse effect.
record.note: 15 people per group. Older Japanese adults with a diagnosed condition, so it says little about healthy people or Black adults.
